title: Anthropic Stock Crashes 9% in $4 Trillion AI Wipeout on Nasdaq
summary: Anthropic stock crashed 9% on Day 2, triggering a trillion AI selloff. Nasdaq erased all 2026 gains. What the crash means for AI builders and startup funding.

Anthropic Stock Crash


# Anthropic Stock Crashes 9% in $4 Trillion AI Wipeout on Nasdaq


By OpenTools Team


·


November 21, 2026


Anthropic shares fell 9% on their second day of trading, dragging the Nasdaq down 5.3% and wiping out all 2026 gains. The selloff erased $4 trillion in market value this week — raising hard questions for AI builders about whether the funding environment that created countless AI tools is about to change.


## The Crash by the Numbers


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's second day as a public company was a bloodbath. Shares of the Claude maker **closed at $88.91, down 8.5%** from Thursday's close — and at one point traded as low as $83.05, just five cents above the $83 IPO price, according to[The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-11-20-2026) .


That's a brutal reversal from Thursday's debut, when the stock opened at $111.50 — 34% above the IPO price — and closed at $97.17. The entire first-day pop has now been wiped out.


But Anthropic was just the fuse. The tech-heavy **Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.28%** on Friday, erasing all gains for 2026 and closing down roughly 2% for the year,[CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/20/investing/us-stocks-anthropic-ai) reported. The S&P 500 fell 3.7%, logging its seventh consecutive day of losses — the longest losing streak since February 2020. The Dow dropped 950 points, or 1.93%.


## A $4 Trillion Wipeout — and Nvidia Bears the Brunt


The scale of the destruction is staggering. **Nasdaq-listed companies lost more than $4 trillion in market value this week** , according to[WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/anthropics-ipo-bust-punctuates-4-trillion-ai-wipeout-on-wall-street-f1f1ec90) . Since its all-time high on October 6, the Nasdaq has shed roughly $8.7 trillion.


[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) was ground[zero](https://opentools.ai/tools/zero-language) for the pain. The chip giant fell 14% on Friday alone and finished the week down 23% — its worst week since the 2008 financial crisis, per[WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-11-20-2026/card/nvidia-stock-is-having-its-worst-week-since-2018-jIhbOst83m4aksKYQ5YK) . Nvidia has now lost more than $1.6 trillion in market cap from its all-time high,[Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/20/anthropic-stock-fall-ipo-ai) noted.


The pain wasn't confined to U.S. markets. Taiwan's TSMCC fell 6%, SoftBank dropped 14.5% in Tokyo, and South Korea's Kospi sank 5.2%,[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/20/glbal-stock-markets-slump-anthropic-ipo-ai-sell-off) reported. "It's a meltdown right now," Arun Sundaram, senior vice president of investment strategy at CFRAA Research, told CNN. "So much bearish sentiment around tech and AI."


## What Triggered the Selloff


The crash wasn't about[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's fundamentals — the company just raised $93.5 billion. It was about **growing investor anxiety over whether AI spending can ever deliver returns** that justify the trillions being poured into infrastructure.


"The AI buildout still needs vast amounts of funding just as financing costs are rising and signs of credit stress are emerging," Swisquote analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya told[WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-11-20-2026) .


The timing couldn't be worse. The selloff was already underway before Anthropic's debut — the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both fell more than 2% on Thursday, **Anthropic's own IPO day. Jensen Huang's shock ouster from[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) earlier in the week had already rattled confidence, and Democratic midterm victories added political uncertainty.**


**"The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, told[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/20/glbal-stock-markets-slump-anthropic-ipo-ai-sell-off) .**


## **Anthropic Has $93.5 Billion — but $2 Trillion in Expectations**


**Here's the paradox: **[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) is now one of the most cash-rich companies on the planet. The underwriters exercised the full greenshoe" overallotment, bringing the total IPO raise to $93.5 billion — selling 1.127 billion shares at $83 each,[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/anthropic-ipo-greenshoe.html) reported. Add the $26 billion private placement from AMD,[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) ,[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) , Nvidia and others, and gross proceeds hit $119.5 billion before expenses.****


****But the market valued Anthropic at roughly $1.5 trillion at IPO, and that valuation now looks increasingly fragile. Neil Wilson, a U.K. investor strategist at Saxo, warned: "Anthropic shares tumbed to take an $85 handle as the post-IPO euphoria gives way to the reality of a steep sell-off across the tech and AI space that shows no sign of easing just yet,"[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/20/glbal-stock-markets-slump-anthropic-ipo-ai-sell-off) quoted.****


## ****What This Means for AI Builders****


****The immediate question for developers and founders building on AI: **is the funding spigot about to close?******


****If the AI trade continues to unravel, several things could happen quickly:****


- ******Startup funding tightens. Venture capital firms mark their portfolios to public comps. When[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) trades at a discount, it compresses valuations for every private AI company.******
- ********Infrastructure costs become harder to justify.** Companies spending millions on GPU compute may face tougher questions from boards and investors about ROI timelines.******
- ******Claude development could slow.** While Anthropic has $93.5 billion in cash, public companies face quarterly earnings pressure. If the stock keeps falling, management may be forced to prioritize revenue growth over research moonshots.****
- ******Open-source and smaller players could benefit.** When capital gets expensive, cheap alternatives become more attractive. Models from Mistral,[Meta](https://opentools.ai/organizations/meta) 's Llama, and the open-source ecosystem may see increased adoption.****


****"This is a painful tech sell-off," tech analyst Dan Ives wrote Friday,[Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/20/anthropic-stock-fall-ipo-ai) reported. The question is whether it's a buying opportunity or the beginning of something larger.****


## ****Is This the AI Top? Wall Street Is Split****


****Analysts are divided on whether this is a healthy correction or the end of the AI boom.****


******The bear case:** AI stocks have lost over 50% of their value in five months, according to Fortune's analysis.[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) "is on pace to have one of the most embarrassing IPOs in history," one investor wrote on Substack,[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-friday-november-19-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-anthropic-nvidia-141644188.html) reported. The valuation multiples that supported AI companies were built on revenue projections that now look increasingly optimistic.****


******The bull case:** Anthropic just generated $93.5 billion in real cash. The company powers millions of developer workflows through Claude. AI adoption is still accelerating — the public market just got ahead of itself on timing.****


****Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG, noted that Anthropic could be "draining market liquidity" as investors sell other stocks to buy into the IPO — meaning some of the selling is mechanical, not fundamental,[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/20/glbal-stock-markets-slump-anthropic-ipo-ai-sell-off) reported.****


## ****What to Watch Next****


****The next few weeks will be critical for the AI market. Key signals for builders to monitor:****


- ******[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's first earnings report as a public company.** Revenue growth, Claude usage metrics, and enterprise adoption numbers will either validate or undermine the $1.5 trillion valuation.****
- ******[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) earnings.** The chipmaker's next quarterly report is the single most important data point for the AI trade. If demand is softening, expect another leg down.****
- ******Rate decisions.** Rising financing costs make big AI bets harder to justify. If central banks signal further rate hikes, the selloff could accelerate.****
- ******The IPO pipeline.** Other AI companies were watching Anthropic as a bellwether. If ANT keeps falling, expect delayed or downsized IPOs across the sector.****


****The market's message is clear: record-breaking IPO» and $93.5 billion raises are no longer enough to overcome fear that AI spending has outpaced real-world returns. For builders, that means the era of infinite AI capital may be ending — and the era of needing to show real utility is just beginning.****
